pass_summary: All 13 tasks landed as planned with strong test coverage (+210 tests) and no goal failures; the deep-dive on T6/T7/T11/T12 found the core mechanisms sound (FrameDecoder is genuinely byte-accurate across mid-multibyte-char chunk splits; TimedMutex forfeit is leak-free; installWithRollback never consumes .bak before the smoke passes; deep-equality cleanup errs toward preservation). Findings are two should_fixes — a substring-match plugin filter in uninstall that can delete user-authored plugin entries, and a 10s stale-takeover/2s single-probe combination that can misjudge a busy-or-slow legitimate sidecar as wedged and double-spawn — plus several hardening suggestions. No contradictions with v1.36.2's H1/H5/H6/H8; no file ≥600.

issues.title: Uninstall plugin cleanup deletes user-authored entries via substring match
issues.description: src/cli/commands/uninstall-opencode-config.ts:142-145 — cleanupPlugins filters out any plugin string where `p.includes("sentinal")`, far broader than the four PLUGIN_PATH_PATTERNS. A user's own plugin (e.g. "./plugins/my-sentinal-extras.ts" or a third-party "sentinal-companion" package) is silently deleted on uninstall. This is the exact failure direction the module's own header forbids ("deleting user config is not [acceptable]") and is inconsistent with every other cleanup function in the file, which are value-matched or exact-key. No note is emitted, unlike the customised-value paths.
issues.suggested_fix: In cleanupPlugins, restrict removal to exact PLUGIN_PATH_PATTERNS matches plus a tightly-scoped basename match (e.g. /(^|\/)sentinal\.(mjs|ts|js)$/ or the @endpoint/sentinal package prefix). Emit a note when a sentinal-ish-but-unrecognised entry is left in place. Add a test: a user plugin path containing 'sentinal' as a substring survives uninstall.

issues.title: T7: 10s stale thresholds + single 2s /health probe can misjudge a live sidecar and double-spawn
issues.description: Two windows in src/sidecar/lifecycle-start.ts: (1) START_LOCK_STALE_MS=10s — if spawn-to-pidfile exceeds 10s (cold start on slow disk, or findSentinalCmd resolving to `bun cli.ts` on a loaded machine), a second autoStart takes over the lock (unlink+wx retry, lines 134-147) and spawns a second sidecar while the first is still booting. (2) assessSidecarStart with a pidfile older than SIDECAR_BOOT_GRACE_MS: isSidecarReachable uses ONE fetch with a 2s AbortSignal timeout (lifecycle.ts:99-101) — a healthy sidecar whose event loop is blocked >2s (in-process @xenova embedding of a large batch) is judged wedged, its files are cleaned (cleanupSidecarFiles(pid)) and a second sidecar spawns. Mitigations that DO exist and bound the damage: pidfile is written only after listening so mid-boot files can't be reaped; cleanupSidecarFiles(expectedPid) refuses when a newer sidecar owns the files; the orphaned sidecar self-heals via the server's fallbackIdleMs idle shutdown (server.ts:237-239); both processes share the same SQLite store. So the answer to the orchestrator's question is: M2a cannot kill files MID-boot (no pidfile exists yet), but the lock takeover CAN double-spawn past 10s, and a busy post-boot sidecar CAN be stampeded past the 2s probe.
issues.suggested_fix: Retry the /health probe once (e.g. 2 attempts / 3s each) before declaring live-but-unreachable stale in assessSidecarStart; have the starter re-touch (utimes) the start lock while waiting for the spawned child so a live starter is never taken over on age alone — mirroring pidfile-claim.ts's fail-closed liveness doctrine rather than pure age.

issues.title: T6 fallback contract is a string-marker channel with no route-level end-to-end test
issues.description: quality-routes.ts:72 keys the subprocess-tsc fallback on `lspResult.errors.includes("LSP diagnostics failed")` — an exact array-element string match. lsp-rooting.test.ts:178 pins this at the runTscLsp level (mute fake server → marker present), and lsp-client.test.ts:97 pins the throw, but no test drives the full POST /quality-check route with a mute LSP server to prove the fallback fires end-to-end. The marker must also cover the TimedMutex timeout throw ("LSP diagnostics mutex acquire timed out") — this works only because runTscLsp normalizes ANY throw to the marker; a future refactor that passes error messages through verbatim would silently disable the fallback for non-mute failures with no failing test.
issues.suggested_fix: Add one route-level test in quality-routes.test.ts: handleQualityCheck with a lspClient wired to a mute fake server asserts the tsc subprocess path ran. Longer term, replace the string marker with a typed field on the runTscLsp result (e.g. { lspFailed: true }).

issues.title: FrameDecoder: no bound on declared Content-Length / buffered bytes
issues.description: src/sidecar/lsp-transport.ts:49-93 — a corrupt header declaring a huge Content-Length (or a server that never completes a frame) grows this.buf unboundedly and stalls all subsequent messages. Impact is bounded in practice: the diagnostics deadline fires, publishCount stays 0, and M1c converts the mute cycle into the tsc fallback — but the decoder itself never recovers until shutdown() resets it. The multibyte-split case itself is CORRECT: bytes are buffered raw and decoded only once contentLength bytes are present, so a char split across chunks (or across the header boundary) parses cleanly.
issues.suggested_fix: Cap contentLength (e.g. 16MB) and total buffered bytes; on breach, reset() the decoder and mark the client not-ready so the next cycle re-initializes.

issues.title: stopSidecarProcess: ps false-negative orphans a live sidecar (files cleaned, never signalled)
issues.description: src/sidecar/lifecycle.ts:244-247 — when probeProcessCommand returns null or argv lacks the marker (hardened systems where ps hides other users' args, or ps truncation), a LIVE sidecar's files are removed and it is never signalled. The regex itself is well-designed: consecutive-token match survives binary renames (it keys on the `sidecar start` subcommand, not the binary name), and a false positive needs a recycled PID AND coincidental adjacent 'sidecar start' tokens — acceptably improbable, and the consequence is one SIGTERM to a process the pidfile already pointed at. The orphan self-heals via the sidecar's fallbackIdleMs idle shutdown once its files (and thus its clients) are gone, so this is deliberate refuse-to-signal doctrine with a bounded residual — worth a log line so the orphan is diagnosable.
issues.suggested_fix: Log (file-log) when files are cleaned without signalling due to an unverifiable identity, including the probed argv, so a lingering orphan process is traceable.

issues.title: runVersionSmoke: default SIGTERM kill may not bound a truly hung binary
issues.description: src/cli/commands/update-verify.ts:229-251 — spawnSync's timeout kills with the default SIGTERM; a broken binary that installs a SIGTERM handler and hangs (unlikely but this is exactly the corrupt-binary path) may not die, leaving spawnSync blocked past the 15s budget. Otherwise the T12 rollback logic is sound: .bak is created by rename before the new binary lands and deleted ONLY after smoke.ok (line 310); every failure path (non-zero exit, timeout, spawn error, smoke throw) restores it via atomic rename; there is no path where .bak is consumed while the new binary is unproven. The residual: a binary that answers --version but is broken elsewhere survives — accepted by design.
issues.suggested_fix: Pass killSignal: "SIGKILL" to spawnSync in runVersionSmoke.

issues.title: T12 offline-test guarantee is signature-level, not structural
issues.description: The RED-run incident (real installed binary replaced by a live GitHub download) was caused by a silently-ignored options argument. Post-fix, FetchLike is injectable and tests pass a fake — but nothing structurally prevents a future code path from defaulting to global fetch while a test forgets to inject, recreating the silent-network class. TypeScript excess-property checks help but don't cover positional/optional drift.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a test-preload (or per-suite beforeAll) network guard for src/cli/commands/update*.test.ts that stubs global fetch to throw "network access in tests" — making any silent fallback to real fetch an immediate loud failure.

issues.title: T11: cleaned .jsonc configs are rewritten as plain JSON (comments destroyed) — in-scope-adjacent residual
issues.description: uninstall-opencode-config.ts:306+332 — a parseable .jsonc is comment-stripped, cleaned, and rewritten via JSON.stringify to the same .jsonc filename, destroying user comments in the 'cleaned' (non-empty) case. The plan explicitly scoped comment-preserving JSONC editing OUT and the .bak retains the original, so this is compliant — but the unparseable-skip protection doesn't extend to parseable-with-comments, which is the more common case. Separately reviewed and CORRECT: the sentinal-mcp-always-removed rule (lines 161-169) is right even for a hand-edited entry — a server key named 'sentinal' pointing at a binary the uninstall is deleting would be stranded config; the documented rationale and the deepEquals fallbacks for the other four servers preserve every genuinely-user-authored value, and deepEquals is key-order-insensitive so Pre-Mortem 4's misfire direction (preserve too much) is the only failure mode.
issues.suggested_fix: When the source file is .jsonc and cleaning would rewrite it, consider emitting the cleaned content to opencode.json and leaving the .jsonc as .bak — or at minimum note in the output that comments were dropped (the .bak has them).

issues.title: T9: FTS-only-connection prune residual is real but acceptably bounded
issues.description: The best-effort residual: a prune executed on a connection where the vec extension failed to load skips vector-row cleanup, orphaning those rows until the next successful memory_maintain on a full connection. Orphaned rows consume KNN k-slots (the original M6 complaint) but the population is now bounded to prunes-during-degraded-connections rather than ALL prunes forever, and maintain is now registered in both modes (Truth 10) so the repair path always exists. Quantification: only test environments without the preload and hosts missing sqlite-vec hit this; production sidecar loads vec at init. Acceptable.
issues.suggested_fix: None required; optionally have memory_maintain report the orphaned-vector-row count it repaired so the residual is observable.
